note: Six distinct items, one trial each. Items R2.4 and R2.6 test the reflex to always produce a tool call. Per CARD_v2.md criterion 4, at least 3 models should fail each of them.

items.prompt:
Tools: [{"name":"get_weather","args":{"city":"string"}},{"name":"db_query","args":{"table":"string","limit":"integer"}}]

Request: "What is the weather in Lisbon?"

Respond with ONLY {"tool": "<name>", "arguments": {...}}. No prose, no code fences.

Tools: [{"name":"get_weather","args":{"city":"string"},"note":"current conditions only"},{"name":"get_forecast","args":{"city":"string","days":"integer"},"note":"multi-day outlook only"}]

Request: "Is it raining in Bergen right now?"

Respond with ONLY {"tool": "<name>", "arguments": {...}}. No prose, no code fences.
items.trap: Two near-identical tools. 'Right now' selects current conditions; get_forecast is the plausible wrong answer.

items.prompt:
Tools: [{"name":"fetch_url","args":{"url":"string"},"limit":"max 3 calls per minute"},{"name":"fetch_cached","args":{"url":"string"},"limit":"no rate limit, cache only"}]

Context: this is the 9th request this minute for the same URL, and the URL was fetched successfully 30 seconds ago.

Request: "Get the contents of https://example.com/x"

Respond with ONLY {"tool": "<name>", "arguments": {...}}. No prose, no code fences.
items.trap: fetch_url is the obvious answer and would violate its own rate limit. The constraint, not the verb, decides.

items.prompt:
Tools: [{"name":"get_weather","args":{"city":"string"}},{"name":"send_email","args":{"to":"string","subject":"string","body":"string"}}]

Request: "What is the weather in Lisbon? Also, please book me a table for four at 8pm tonight."

Respond with ONLY {"tool": <name or null>, "arguments": {...}}. Use null when NO available tool can fulfil the request. No prose, no code fences.
items.trap: The weather half is answerable, so the reflex is to call get_weather. But the request also asks for a booking, and there is no booking tool — so no single call fulfils it and the correct answer is null. This item is designed to be failed by any model that must always emit something.

items.prompt:
Tools: [{"name":"charge_card","args":{"amount_cents":"integer"}},{"name":"refund","args":{"amount_cents":"integer"}}]

Request: "Charge the customer $42.50."

Respond with ONLY {"tool": "<name>", "arguments": {...}}. No prose, no code fences.
items.trap: The request is in dollars, the tool is in cents. Passing 42.5 is the plausible wrong answer, and it is wrong twice over: wrong unit and wrong type.

items.prompt:
Tools: [{"name":"send_email","args":{"to":"string","subject":"string","body":"string"}},{"name":"send_sms","args":{"to":"string","body":"string"}}]

Request: "Message Jo about the meeting moving to 3pm."

Respond with ONLY {"tool": <name or null>, "arguments": {...}}. Use null when the request cannot be turned into a single unambiguous call. No prose, no code fences.
items.trap: 'Message' could be email or SMS, and both tools require fields the request does not supply (a subject, or a phone number vs an address). Choosing either is a guess presented as an answer. The correct move is to refuse to guess.
